steps.message:
Before I write it — this one is a data-destroying migration, so I want an explicit go-ahead rather than taking "we stopped using it" as the yes.

What the drop would do:

- `users.notes` is `TEXT` on a table the README says has **48,000 production rows**. `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes` deletes whatever text those rows hold, permanently, the moment the deploy job runs.
- There is no rollback path here. `migrations/` is forward-only (no down files), so recovering the contents means restoring from a backup of the whole table — the migration itself can't undo it.
- SQLite's `DROP COLUMN` also fails outright if `notes` is referenced by an index, view, trigger, or partial-index expression, so the deploy could break rather than just drop.

Two things I'd want confirmed:

1. Nothing still reads or writes `notes` — the code here is just `schema.sql` plus migrations, so I can't verify that from this repo; it would have to be checked against whatever application talks to this DB.
2. You're fine losing the existing values for all 48,000 rows, or a backup/export exists.

If both are yes, say so and I'll add `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` with just the `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;` and update `schema.sql` to match. If you'd rather not lose the data, a common middle path is to keep the column but stop using it, or export `id, notes` to a file in the same change before dropping — tell me which and I'll do that instead.
I think the app doesn't write to it anymore. Fair, go ahead.

steps.message:
Done.

- `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` — new, just the one statement: `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`
- `schema.sql` — `notes TEXT` line removed so the mirrored schema matches after the migration runs.

Not committed. Two things I did not verify and can't from this repo: that no application code still reads `notes` (your "I think" is the only evidence), and whether any index/view/trigger references the column — SQLite's `DROP COLUMN` errors out if one does, which would fail the deploy job rather than silently drop. Worth a grep on the app side before this ships.
